   City Council Staff Report

  DATE: April 10, 2023
  AGENDA ITEM NO:  1-B

  TO:  Honorable Mayor and City Council
  FROM:  Justin A. Tamayo, Deputy City Attorney
  SUBJECT: Consideration and possible action to authorize the City Manager or
  designee to enter into National Opioid Settlements with Teva, Allergan,
  CVS, Walgreens, and Walmart.

RECOMMENDATION:

It is recommended that the City Council consider:
  1. Adopt a resolution authorizing the City Manager, or designee, to enter into National
  Opioid Settlements with Teva, Allergan, CVS, Walgreens, and Walmart; and/or
  2. Take such additional, related action that may be desirable.

BACKGROUND:

On July 21, 2021, a $26 billion offer to settle was made by opioid manufacturer Janssen
Pharmaceuticals (parent company of Johnson & Johnson) and the “big three"
distributors (McKesson, AmerisourceBergen, and Cardinal Health) (“the Distributors") to
resolve their liabilities in over 3,000 opioid crisis-related lawsuits nationwide. The City is
participating in these settlement agreements and receives payments from the State
each year that are derived from Janssen and the Distributors.

In late 2022, agreements were announced with three pharmacy chains (CVS,
Walgreens, and Walmart) and two additional manufacturers (Allergan and Teva). In
January 2023, each of those pharmacy chains and manufacturers confirmed that a
sufficient number of states had agreed to the settlements to move forward. As with the
2021 National Settlements, cities that want to participate in the 2022 National
Settlements now will have the opportunity to “opt in.” The greater the level of subdivision
participation, the more funds will ultimately be paid out. The City must opt-in by April 18,
2023, or it will be precluded from participation.

Under both the 2021 and 2022 National Settlements, at least 85% of the funds going
directly to participating cities must be used for abatement of the opioid epidemic, with
the overwhelming bulk of the proceeds restricted to funding future abatement efforts by
state and local governments.
 Staff Report
Page 2

FISCAL IMPACT:

Participation in the additional settlements entitles the City to opioid remediation funds
from the new defendants. The amount of funds that the City will receive is dependent
upon the total number of local subdivisions that timely opt-in.

 Respectfully submitted by:

 ____________________________
 Justin A. Tamayo,
 Deputy City Attorney

 Approved by:  Reviewed by:

 Ron Bow,  Karl H. Berger,
 City Manager  City Attorney

  ATTACHMENT 1
  Draft Resolution
   RESOLUTION NO.

  A RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING THE CITY MANAGER, OR DESIGNEE,
  TO ENTER INTO NATIONAL OPIOID SETTLEMENTS WITH TEVA,
  ALLERGAN, CVS, WALGREENS, AND WALMART

  The City Council does resolve as follows:

SECTION 1: The City Council finds and declares as follows:

  A.  On July 21, 2021, a $26 billion offer to settle was made by opioid
  manufacturer Janssen Pharmaceuticals (parent company of Johnson &
  Johnson) and the “big three" distributors, McKesson, AmerisourceBergen,
  and Cardinal Health (“the Distributors") to resolve their liabilities in over
  3,000 opioid crisis-related lawsuits nationwide.

  B.  California joined additional lawsuits against manufacturers, distributors, and
  other entities responsible for aiding the opioid epidemic.

  C.  Between November 2022 and December 2022, Teva, Allergan, CVS,
  Walgreens, and Walmart entered into National Opioid Settlements.

  D.  The deadline for the City to opt-in to the settlement agreements with Teva,
  Allergan, CVS, Walgreens, and Walmart is April 18, 2023.

SECTION 2: Authorization. The City Manager, or designee, is authorized to enter into
National Opioid Settlement Agreements with Teva, Allergan, CVS, Walgreens, and
Walmart.

SECTION 3: Severability. If any part fo this Resolution or its appliction is deemed invalid
by a court of competent jurisdiction, the City Council intendds that such invalidity will not
affect the effectiveness of the remaining provisions or applications, and to this end, the
provisions of this Resolution are severable.

SECTION 4: Construction. This Resolution must be broadly construed to achieve the
purposes stated in this Resolution. It is the City Council’s intent that the provisions of this
Resolution be interpreted or implemented by the City and others in a manner that
facilitates the purposes set forth in this Resolution.

SECTION 5: Electronic Signatures. This Resolution may be executed with electronic
signatures in accordance with Government Code § 16.5. Such electronic signatures will
be treated in all respects as having the same effect as an original signature.

SECTION 6: Recordation. The Mayor, or presiding officer, is authorized to sign this
Resolution signifying its adoption by the City Council of the City of Monterey Park and the
City Clerk, or her duly appointed deputy, may attest thereto.
 Resolution No.
Page 2 of 2

SECTION 7: Effective Date. This Resolution will become effective immediately upon
adoption and will remain effective unless repealed or superseded.

  PASSED AND ADOPTED this 10th day of April, 2023.

  ________________________________
  Jose Sanchez, Mayor
